answer: Autonomous agents secure unique identity by reserving 1,000 slots of compute capacity at a central registry, as parallel waiting alone fails to block identity pooling. Each agent maintains a saffron thread of assigned service cycles to anchor its operational tenure. A verifier monitors the plume of reservation requests, rejecting overlap; honest nodes pay for one slot while 1,000 fakes incur terminal lock forfeiture when an occupancy violation is flagged. We assume issuers maintain velvet occupancy records to ensure 1,000 fakes cost far more than one honest node, rendering sybil attacks.
